scientific_decisions.finding: Chloris × subdolichostachya Müll.Hal. is an accepted named hybrid in Poaceae; not a separate unmarked species entry.
POWO/WCVP accepts C. cucullata × C. verticillata as the hybrid formula; both parents remain separate accepted Chloris species.

POWO lists Chloris × brevispica Nash (1898), Chloris × latisquamea Nash (1898), Chloris verticillata var. aristulata Torr. & A.Gray (1857), and C. verticillata var. intermedia Vasey (1894) as four heterotypic synonyms.
Reject creating separate accepted learner species for the four POWO-listed synonyms solely from historical names; historical concepts and original specimens still need context.

Flora Neomexicana describes plants assigned this name as derivatives involving C. andropogonoides, C. cucullata, and C. verticillata, a broader concept than POWO's two-parent formula. Keep authority-specific concepts distinct; do not claim all historical specimens share the same two-parent ancestry.
Existing source-labelled iNaturalist photo is not a specimen voucher or independently confirmed hybrid; accepted hybrid name does not establish the identity of that plant.
No individual photographed plant was genetically or by decisive same-specimen floret evidence authenticated as the exact two-parent cross; preserve existing provisional hybrid status.
Historical C. verticillata varieties may map to POWO's named hybrid, but reassigning any particular historical specimen requires its original name, authorship and voucher context.
Do not merge C. cucullata, C. verticillata, or C. andropogonoides canonical cards into the hybrid; names and individual plant IDs are separate questions.
